messages:
incident-bot: P0 ALERT — elevated 5xx/error rate detected for tenant 'acme-corp' in dedicated pool (dc-us-east-2). Paging @Maya K and @eng-sre-oncall. Dashboard: https://redwood.prod/d/ops/tenant-dedicated
Maya K: I'm on the page. Confirming spike — per-tenant 5xx up to ~18% over last 5m, latency also climbing. Only affects acme-corp.
Arjun S: Joining. Quick check: traces for acme-corp are absent in Jaeger — searches return nothing for recent trace IDs. Also, central logs (ELK) show no documents from the acme-dedicated forwarder since ~14:58 UTC.
Maya K: That explains why we can't tie errors to a slow downstream. Do we have node-level request logs on the pool?
infra-bot: Pool nodes show healthy CPU/mem. log-forwarder for tenant acme-corp reports repeated TLS handshake failures to log-collector.us-east.prod:443. Sample error:
```
2024-06-11T15:12:03Z forwarder[acme-corp] TLS handshake error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```
Priya N: Sounds like a cert rotation issue for tenant-managed certs. Acme uses a customer-provided cert/provisioning process in their VPC peering — that could break the forwarder handshake.
Tom L: (Account) I spoke to Acme SRE — they did a cert rotate last night and reported transient failures, assumed fallback would cover. They've opened a ticket on their side: ACME-457. They can re-run the bootstrap if we ask.
Arjun S: Additional complication: our observability for dedicated tenants is partially partitioned. The trace index for Private/Dedicated tenants lives in a tenant-scoped storage layer (for isolation). For this pool we only get aggregated metrics forwarded to central dashboards; when traces/logs are missing we can't reconstruct request->span joins. That leaves us with metric-level symptoms only.
Maya K: Immediate mitigations proposed: 1) throttle/limit acme-corp traffic to reduce error amplification. 2) enable fallback routing for non-sensitive requests to hosted-shared pool. 3) coordinate with Acme to re-provision certs or allow temporary collector exception. Which can we do now?
Arjun S: I can apply a tenant-level rate-limit quickly. Patch I'm about to run from eng-ops (applies to the dedicated pool):
```
kubectl --context=cluster-dedicated-acme patch configmap rate-limits -p '{"data":{"tenant_acme_rate":"50r/s"}}'
```
I'll run now and watch.
Maya K: Tom, ask Acme to re-run the cert bootstrap and confirm collector CN and CA chain. If they can't re-run quickly, Priya — can Security allow a temporary exception on collector auth restricted by source IP?
Priya N: I'll review. Temporary exception acceptable with conditions: 1) restrict to pool IPs, 2) 15min window, 3) enhanced audit logging. Need sign-off from legal & infra but can do emergency policy. I will coordinate.
support-bot: Customer impact summary: Acme experiencing ~35% failed generation requests (502/504) in current window. No other tenants reported. SLA threshold breach risk if sustained.
Arjun S: Rate-limit applied. Also toggled fallback routing (non-authenticated/read-only paths) to hosted-shared pool to reduce user-visible failures. Early signal: 5xx dropped from 18% -> ~7% within 4m.
Maya K: Good. Remaining issue: missing per-tenant traces/logs — until that's fixed, post-incident RCA will be limited. Long-term fixes: make forwarder cert rotation resilient, or mirror VPC tenant logs to central observability (opt-in). Priya, can you file remediation tickets?
Priya N: Done. Created INF-4228: "forwarder cert rotation handling (tenant VPC)" and OBS-1192: "opt-in mirror pipeline for VPC/dedicated tenant logs to central ELK". Assigned to infra and observability.
Tom L: I'll prepare a customer-facing note: high level, root cause tied to log-forwarder TLS after customer cert rotate; we've applied rate-limits and temporary fallback and requested they restart bootstrap. Will propose a follow-up call for deeper RCA.
Maya K: Handoff plan: I'll stay on mitigation for 30m and then hand to Arjun for long dive & postmortem. Arjun will own RCA and ticket linking. Tom will own customer comms. Priya will own security exception if needed.
Arjun S: I'll take the handoff at 1729007000 and start gathering traces from node-level sockets and any remaining forwarder buffers. Will draft initial timeline for RCA.
Maya K: Thanks. Final note: we should treat this as a class of risk for enterprise VPC/dedicated customers — observability partitions + customer-managed certs is a dangerous combo. Need product/infra discussion on providing safer rollouts and clearer operator guidance. I'll add this to the post-incident review. :thumbsup:
Maya K: Handoff complete. Posting postmortem link when ready.
